A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenMol and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renamed and relocated material can be reliably matched across the versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original GenMol experiments on de novo generation, fragment-constrained generation, PMO optimization, and docking-based lead optimization, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original GenMol experiments and adds guidance evaluations, comparison methods, and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: V2 introduces molecular context guidance (MCG), which combines predictions from the current sequence and a further-masked sequence to modify inference logits (Section 4.3). The BERT/MDLM backbone and fragment remasking remain; expanded documentation of fragment scoring and decomposition does not itself establish further procedural changes.

E1.justification: The added DiGress comparisons introduce a GuacaMol-trained model (Appendix E.1). The four task families, ten-drug fragment benchmark, 23 PMO objectives, and five lead-optimization targets remain. Newly identifying DUD-E and ChEMBL documents the retained seeds' provenance rather than establishing new target coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds JT-VAE and DiGress to de novo comparisons, DiGress to fragment-constrained comparisons, and standard-diffusion and GPT-remasking controls. SELFIES-REINVENT and GP BO in the main PMO table were already in v1's appendix. GenMol-TR and GenMol-NR are retained under new names.

E3.justification: V2 adds guidance searches with w=2 and gamma from 0 to 0.5, a ten-fragment initialization condition, and alternative QED/SA thresholds. Table 1 also replaces one temperature/randomness configuration. Main training budgets, generation counts, and the 10,000-call PMO budget remain; 15 versus 30 lead tasks counts the same seeds under two similarity thresholds.

E4.justification: New analyses test confidence sampling, diffusion versus GPT fragment regeneration, MCG, quality-threshold sensitivity, and reduced fragment availability. Conversely, the GenMol-ZINC250k training studies disappear, and lead-remasking ablations retain only delta=0.4 rather than both similarity thresholds. Existing token/no-remasking controls are renamed, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 Tables 4 and 17 newly describe lead-optimization scores as means over three runs; v1 did not specify this aggregation or run count. This does not establish an increase in runs. Other experiments retain three-run mean/standard-deviation reporting, and lead-score dispersion remains unreported.

E6.justification: The new MCG variant reports PMO sum 18.362 versus the retained unguided 18.208, and motif-extension quality 30.1% versus 27.5%. V2 adds baseline, sensitivity, and ten-fragment results while removing ZINC250k-trained results. Lead scores also change under newly specified aggregation; v2 Tables 4 and 17 disagree for the guided 5ht1b seed -9.8 at delta=0.4 (-11.6 versus -11.8).

T1.justification: Beyond v1's masked-diffusion background, v2 adds a CTMC-based derivation of MCG in Appendix C, a formal fragment-scoring definition, and a Gibbs-sampling formulation of fragment remasking in Section 4.2. These extend the mathematical content beyond notation or explanatory restatement.

C1.justification: MCG becomes an additional central contribution in the abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion. The generalist-generation claims remain, while statements that parallel decoding improves efficiency without degrading quality are removed.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges the quality loss from unmasking multiple tokens and the assumption of a supplied high-quality fragment vocabulary. It also adds Gibbs-sampling and context-calibration explanations and interprets the new GPT-remasking control. These materially qualify applicability and expand the account of why the method works.

D1.justification: Section 4.2, Algorithm 1, and Appendix D newly specify fragment scoring and selection, distinct decomposition rules, unlimited lead vocabulary size, seed provenance, SAFE split counts, and guidance settings. Baseline implementation links are added, and reported training time changes from approximately six to five hours.

R1.justification: V2 positions MCG relative to Karras et al.'s autoguidance and Nisonoff et al.'s discrete guidance, and adds Gibbs-sampling, fragment-design, and dataset references. Bohacek et al. and Tang et al. are removed. The broader positioning around SAFE, discrete diffusion, and generalist molecular generation remains.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 is reorganized around scoring, attaching, and remasking; confidence-sampling details move to Appendix B; and the appendices are reorganized into A–E. The abstract, introduction, baseline descriptions, and ablation narrative are also substantially reworked.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with explicit axis scales, and the lead-results table is restructured beside a new ablation summary. V2 adds Algorithm 1, dataset and parameter tables, baseline and sensitivity displays, and molecular examples in Figures 7–8. Detailed ablations are reorganized into appendix tables.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves reproducibility and tests the method's explanations more directly: Algorithm 1 and Appendix D clarify the previously underspecified fragment pipeline, while new confidence-sampling, GPT-remasking, MCG, and threshold controls strengthen the evidence. Explicit limitations also correct the speed-quality overstatement. These gains outweigh the removed ZINC250k and strict-similarity ablations and the localized lead-score inconsistency between Tables 4 and 17.
